design_decisions: Three observations at Syncthing's roughly two-second cadence provide a four-to-six second settling window for a multi-write save. Freshness continues to exclude reports from before the observed local mutation.

Completion deliberately means the local folder has settled and at least one connected relevant peer has confirmed the content. It does not mean every connected peer has completed, and it never covers disconnected or offline configured peers.
Peer counts, aggregate content need, pending-delete counts, and pending-delete totals remain diagnostics so a completion sample still records lagging peers rather than hiding them.

Debug logging evaluates logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG) at first-peer completion. It can extend backend observation through all-peer completion, the stall boundary, or the hard ceiling, but the published sample and user-visible status remain identical.

The 2026-08-11 Wobbly Life capture is the baseline: peers completed at +15.3s, +19.5s, and +36.3s; the earlier all-peers result published at +39.4s. First-peer confirmation targets about +15.3s plus four-to-six seconds of settling, reducing the approximately 44-second visible strip to roughly 25 seconds including its terminal hide.

review_history: Review 02 corrected a plan defect: Task 2's original halt-and-report instruction gave an agent with no reporting channel no distinguishable way to signal a blocker. Two rounds wrote a valid marker with no code, and neither orchestration status nor recover detected it; the orchestrator found it by comparing the branch diff with the marker.

Review 03 found that frontend stopWatch made debug-extended observation unreachable even though watch-level tests passed. The manager now leaves a debug-extended watch observing while removing it from the replacement-blocking registry.

Review 04 found that a watch removed for replacement escaped stop_all teardown. The manager now tracks debug-observing watches separately, drains that collection during stop_all, and deregisters self-terminated watches.

Review 05 accepts a narrow race: a watch can self-terminate between the extending-state check and manager registration, leaving only a stopped dictionary entry until stop_all. It does not retain a thread or polling loop and is cleared at teardown.

deferred_verification: A post-game device run remains deferred to a prerelease. Its required signature is SYNCTHING COMPLETE while a transition diagnostic still reports incomplete_peers greater than zero, with handoff-to-complete compared to the +39.4-second baseline.
Debug-extended observation is unit-tested but has not run against a live slow peer.

The unchanged 90-second stall window, 900-second backend hard ceiling, and 300-second frontend no-evidence ceiling remain unexercised on device. Completing on the first peer makes those boundaries less likely to be reached, not verified.
The acceptability of the weaker at-least-one-connected-peer guarantee is a product judgement, not a testable fact.
